decisions.reason: Although it fits the bakery's core know-how, a specific bread loaf that was no longer observed on the website in 2020 and 2021 was likely discontinued or absorbed into the standard assortment, so management would treat it as no longer worth dedicated continuation.

The guided historic mill tour builds on the firm's heritage and facilities, but after disappearing from observation for two years and being less central than baked goods, it would be viewed as a peripheral offer with a high likelihood of remaining off the market.

A sweet pastry is well within the firm's absorptive capacity, yet its absence from the website over two years suggests weak distinct positioning or replacement by other pastries, making discontinuation the likely managerial choice.

This farmhouse bread is very close to the firm's established bread-making skills and ingredient base, so in the absence of negative signals management would usually keep it and rely on routine learning and refinement.

The poppy seed Christmas stollen is highly related to the firm's core seasonal specialty competence, was highlighted as a flagship product, and had a gold-award signal, all of which strongly support continued commercialization.

The premium Christmas stollen also sits squarely in the firm's traditional specialty expertise and received a gold-award signal, so management would be inclined to keep it, though with slightly less commitment than the flagship stollen.
